content.intro: In this lesson, you will study understanding java terminology with a short explanation, an original visual map, a Java example, and a check you can perform yourself. Focus on the relationship between the rule and the behavior rather than memorizing isolated syntax.
content.why_it_matters: This concept matters because it helps you recognize the Java language, the JVM, and the JDK as related but distinct parts of a development platform. In this lesson, focus on java development kit (jdk) and use a minimal example to check what the rule actually guarantees.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: The JDK supplies the Java compiler and development tools as well as a runtime. A runtime can execute applications, but compiling and debugging usually require the JDK tools. The important habit is to make the assumptions explicit and use the code example as a small experiment.

content_blocks.title: How the pieces fit
content_blocks.text: Connect java development kit (jdk) with java virtual machine (jvm) before choosing an implementation. The example is a small, observable case; extend it by changing one input and checking a boundary, invalid value, or compatibility limit where relevant.

items.title: Java Development Kit (JDK)
items.text: The JDK supplies the Java compiler and development tools as well as a runtime. A runtime can execute applications, but compiling and debugging usually require the JDK tools.

items.title: Java Virtual Machine (JVM)
items.text: The JVM loads class files, verifies and executes bytecode, manages runtime memory, and may compile hot code for the host processor.

items.title: Java runtime components
items.text: Use the standard library type that matches the data: java.time for dates and zones, BigDecimal for exact decimal arithmetic, and locale-aware APIs for user-facing text and numbers.

items.title: Source code, bytecode, and class files
items.text: Java source is compiled to class-file bytecode that a compatible JVM can execute. Native libraries, file paths, runtime versions, and platform assumptions can still affect portability.

items.title: Standard library and APIs
items.text: Java is a general-purpose, statically typed language and a platform. Source code is compiled into class-file bytecode that a compatible JVM can execute; distinguish the language, JVM, JDK tools, and standard APIs. Apply that reasoning specifically to standard library and apis and confirm the result with the example or a targeted test.

JDK = development tools
JVM = bytecode runtime
content_blocks.run_instructions: Contrast the JDK and JVM terms. For ordinary Java SE examples, use JDK 25, save a complete class as Main.java, and run `javac Main.java` followed by `java Main`. CodeLeaf does not execute Java in the browser; use a local JDK for these examples. Preview-only and configuration-file examples have their own version or filename notes.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original example, remove any temporary output files it created, and rerun the baseline case. Do not leave credentials, generated private data, or large test files in the project directory.

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Keep one clear hypothesis per experiment. Check the version, read the error message, test boundaries, and record what evidence supports your conclusion.

common_mistakes.problem: Applying the rule from memory without checking its exact contract.
common_mistakes.why: Small differences in type, scope, API version, or input shape can change the result.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect the relevant official API/language documentation and build a minimal reproducer.

common_mistakes.problem: Testing only a single happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Boundary values and failures often reveal assumptions hidden by the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add an empty, boundary, or invalid case and state the expected behavior before running it.
